alabama.state_note: SSA lists Alabama's DDS under the state Department of Education, with offices in Birmingham and Mobile. An SSI approval in Alabama also brings Medicaid coverage.

alaska.state_note: Alaska has a single DDS office, in Anchorage, serving the whole state; it sits in the Division of Vocational Rehabilitation within the Department of Labor and Workforce Development.

arizona.state_note: Arizona's DDS is the Disability Determination Services Administration, a division of the Department of Economic Security; it also makes disability determinations for AHCCCS (Medicaid), and Arizona pays no state supplement on top of federal SSI.

arkansas.state_note: Arkansas has a single DDS office, in Little Rock. SSI recipients in Arkansas automatically receive full Medicaid.

california.state_note: California's DDS is the Disability Determination Service Division within the California Department of Social Services. California adds a State Supplementary Payment (SSP) on top of federal SSI, administered by SSA.

colorado.state_note: Colorado's DDS is a division of the Colorado Department of Human Services' Office of Adult, Aging and Disability Services, located in Aurora, and decides about 40,000 claims per year.

connecticut.state_note: Connecticut's DDS sits in the Department of Aging and Disability Services, Bureau of Rehabilitation Services. Connecticut also has a State Supplement program that can add cash assistance for people who are disabled or over 65.

delaware.state_note: Delaware's DDS is part of the Division of Vocational Rehabilitation in the Department of Labor, and it is the only DDS office in the state, located in New Castle.

florida.state_note: Florida's Division of Disability Determinations is run by the Florida Department of Health, and it also decides medical eligibility for Florida's Medically Needy Program. SSI recipients in Florida are automatically enrolled in Medicaid.

georgia.state_note: Georgia does not call its agency DDS; Disability Adjudication Services (DAS) is a division of the Georgia Vocational Rehabilitation Agency, with offices in Stone Mountain, Athens, Savannah, Dalton, and Thomasville.

hawaii.dds_name: Disability Determination Branch, Hawaii Department of Human Services
hawaii.state_note: Hawaii's Disability Determination Branch, in the Department of Human Services, makes the medical decision on SSDI and SSI claims and is 100 percent federally funded by SSA; no standalone official DDB webpage was found, so no DDS URL is listed.

idaho.dds_name: Idaho Disability Determinations Service, Idaho Department of Labor
idaho.state_note: Idaho's DDS is in the Idaho Department of Labor and decides medical eligibility for SSDI and SSI for Idahoans; Idaho also pays a state supplement for SSI recipients living in residential care or assisted-living facilities, administered by the Department of Health and Welfare. No official DDS webpage URL was found in search results, so no DDS URL is listed.

illinois.dds_name: Bureau of Disability Determination Services, Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Rehabilitation Services
illinois.state_note: Illinois' Bureau of Disability Determination Services, in Springfield, makes the medical decision on SSDI and SSI claims; Illinois runs its own SSI supplement, Aid to the Aged, Blind, or Disabled (AABD), through the Department of Human Services, separate from the federal SSI check.

indiana.dds_name: Indiana Disability Determination Bureau, Indiana Family and Social Services Administration
indiana.state_note: Indiana's Disability Determination Bureau, under the Family and Social Services Administration, makes the medical decision on SSDI and SSI claims; applications are filed with SSA, not with the Bureau. No standalone FSSA Bureau webpage URL was found, so the official SSA Chicago-region DDS page is listed instead.

iowa.dds_name: Iowa Disability Determination Services, Iowa Workforce Development
iowa.state_note: Iowa's DDS operates as a division within Iowa Workforce Development; in federal fiscal year 2025 it averaged 80.9 days to process an initial disability claim, compared with a 190-day national average. No official DDS webpage URL was found in search results, so no DDS URL is listed.

kansas.dds_name: Disability Determination Services, Kansas Department for Children and Families
kansas.state_note: Kansas DDS, in the Department for Children and Families, makes disability and blindness determinations for SSA on most SSDI and SSI claims filed in Kansas, and also makes Medicaid eligibility determinations for people who do not meet the financial requirements for SSI.

kentucky.dds_name: Department for Disability Determination Services, Kentucky Education and Labor Cabinet
kentucky.state_note: Kentucky's DDS, under the Education and Labor Cabinet, makes disability determinations for SSA and does not take benefit applications, which are filed with SSA; it also determines medical eligibility for KTAP and Medicaid. Kentucky divides free civil legal aid among four regional programs, and Kentucky Legal Aid covers 35 counties in western and south-central Kentucky.

louisiana.dds_name: Disability Determination Services, Louisiana Department of Health
louisiana.state_note: Louisiana's DDS moved from the Department of Children and Family Services to the Department of Health on October 1, 2025, and has offices in Baton Rouge, New Orleans, and Shreveport; Southeast Louisiana Legal Services covers 22 southeast parishes, while Acadiana Legal Service Corporation covers the other 42 parishes.

maine.dds_name: Disability Determination Services, Maine Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Family Independence
maine.state_note: Maine's single DDS office is in Winthrop, in the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Family Independence; no standalone Maine DHHS DDS webpage URL was found, so the official SSA Boston-region Maine page is listed instead.

maryland.dds_name: Maryland Disability Determination Services, Division of Rehabilitation Services, Maryland State Department of Education
maryland.state_note: Maryland's DDS is a state agency within the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) under the State Department of Education; a person approved for SSI in Maryland is granted Medicaid automatically.

massachusetts.state_note: Massachusetts DDS is part of MassAbility (formerly the Massachusetts Rehabilitation Commission) and is 100% funded by the Social Security Administration, with offices in Everett (Boston area) and Worcester.

michigan.state_note: Michigan's DDS sits in the Department of Health and Human Services and also decides State Disability Assistance and Medicaid disability claims, with offices in Lansing, Detroit, Kalamazoo, and Traverse City; Michigan adds a small state supplement to SSI ($14/month for a person living alone in 2026).

minnesota.state_note: Minnesota's DDS is housed in the Department of Employment and Economic Development (DEED) in St. Paul and is 100% federally funded; Mid-Minnesota Legal Aid is contracted with the Minnesota Department of Human Services to provide free Social Security advocacy, including SSI/SSDI applications, appeals, and hearing representation.

mississippi.state_note: Mississippi's DDS is a single office in Madison under the Mississippi Department of Rehabilitation Services and handles claims from all 23 Social Security field offices in the state; the Mississippi Center for Legal Services lists Social Security Disability and SSI among its case priorities.

missouri.state_note: Missouri's DDS sits under the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education's Office of Adult Learning and Rehabilitation Services, with six offices statewide. Missouri is a 209(b) state, so an SSI approval does not automatically enroll a person in MO HealthNet; a separate Medicaid application is required.

montana.state_note: Montana's DDS (also called the Disability Determination Bureau) is part of the Disability Employment and Transitions Division in the Department of Public Health and Human Services, with a single office in Helena; Montana Legal Services Association lists Social Security Disability among the free civil legal help it provides statewide.

nebraska.state_note: Nebraska's DDS is a division of the Nebraska Department of Education, with a single office in Lincoln. Nebraska pays a state supplement to SSI through the Assistance to the Aged, Blind, or Disabled (AABD) program, run separately from SSA by the Department of Health and Human Services.

nevada.dds_name: Nevada Disability Determination Services (Bureau of Disability Adjudication)
nevada.state_note: Nevada's DDS is called the Bureau of Disability Adjudication and sits in the Department of Employment, Training, and Rehabilitation (DETR), with offices in Carson City and Las Vegas; Nevada Legal Services is a statewide nonprofit that lists Social Security Disability among the government-benefit denials it handles.

new hampshire.state_note: New Hampshire's DDS is administered by the New Hampshire Department of Education, with a single office in Concord. New Hampshire Legal Assistance lists SSDI and SSI denials among the public-benefits cases it handles, and the state also offers Aid to the Permanently and Totally Disabled (APTD) cash assistance for residents ages 18-64.

new jersey.dds_name: New Jersey Division of Disability Determination Services
new jersey.state_note: New Jersey's Division of Disability Determination Services sits in the Department of Labor and Workforce Development and says an initial decision usually takes three to five months. New Jersey adds a small state supplement to SSI that Social Security pays with the federal check, and SSI recipients in New Jersey automatically receive Medicaid.

new mexico.dds_name: New Mexico Disability Determination Services (NMDDS), Division of Vocational Rehabilitation
new mexico.state_note: New Mexico's DDS is part of the New Mexico Division of Vocational Rehabilitation and has a single office in Albuquerque; New Mexico also pays a state supplement to SSI for people living in an adult residential or assisted living facility.

new york.dds_name: Division of Disability Determinations, New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
new york.state_note: New York's disability determinations are made by OTDA's Division of Disability Determinations, and New York runs a State Supplement Program (SSP) that adds state money to the federal SSI payment.

north carolina.dds_name: Disability Determination Services, North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
north carolina.state_note: North Carolina's DDS is a division of the NC Department of Health and Human Services and, unlike most states, also makes medical determinations for state Medicaid disability claims.

north dakota.dds_name: Disability Determination Services, North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services
north dakota.state_note: North Dakota's DDS is a section of the state Department of Health and Human Services in Bismarck, and applications must be submitted through SSA, not directly to DDS.

ohio.dds_name: Division of Disability Determination (DDD), Opportunities for Ohioans with Disabilities (OOD)
ohio.state_note: Ohio's Division of Disability Determination is part of Opportunities for Ohioans with Disabilities, which is the sole state agency that administers SSDI and SSI disability determinations in Ohio.

oklahoma.dds_name: Disability Determination Services, Oklahoma Department of Rehabilitation Services
oklahoma.state_note: Oklahoma's DDS is a division of the Oklahoma Department of Rehabilitation Services and is fully funded by the Social Security Administration.

oregon.dds_name: Disability Determination Services, Oregon Department of Human Services
oregon.state_note: Oregon's DDS is a unit of the Oregon Department of Human Services with its single office in Salem, and Oregon adds a state supplement to SSI for some recipients.

pennsylvania.dds_name: Bureau of Disability Determination (BDD), Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry
pennsylvania.state_note: Pennsylvania's Bureau of Disability Determination is part of the Department of Labor and Industry, and Pennsylvania adds a small state supplement to SSI for some recipients, with an SSI approval also bringing Medicaid automatically.

rhode island.dds_name: Disability Determination Services, Rhode Island Office of Rehabilitation Services (Department of Human Services)
rhode island.state_note: Rhode Island's DDS is a unit within the Office of Rehabilitation Services, and Rhode Island pays extra state money to people receiving SSI in the state.

south carolina.dds_name: Disability Determination Services, South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department
south carolina.state_note: South Carolina's DDS is a unit of the SC Vocational Rehabilitation Department with offices in West Columbia, Charleston, and Greenville, and it also processes Medicaid disability claims and disability retirement claims for the SC Public Employee Benefit Authority.

south dakota.legal_aid_name: SD Law Help (East River Legal Services / Dakota Plains Legal Services)
south dakota.state_note: South Dakota's DDS is administered by the Department of Human Services (Division of Rehabilitation Services) from its Sioux Falls office; claims are filed with SSA first and then sent to DDS for the medical decision.

tennessee.legal_aid_name: Legal Aid Society of Middle Tennessee and the Cumberlands
tennessee.state_note: Tennessee DDS is a section within the Division of Rehabilitation Services of the Department of Human Services and decides SSDI and SSI claims under an agreement with SSA.

texas.dds_name: Texas Disability Determination Services (Division for Disability Determination Services, Texas Health and Human Services Commission)
texas.state_note: Texas DDS operates as a division of the Texas Health and Human Services Commission, with its central office in Austin; in Texas, SSI approval also brings Medicaid enrollment.

utah.state_note: Utah's DDS is administered by the Department of Workforce Services (Utah State Office of Rehabilitation) from Salt Lake City; Utah Legal Services states it may help eligible clients with disability applications, reconsiderations, and hearings before an administrative law judge.

vermont.state_note: Vermont DDS is a division in the Department for Children and Families (Agency of Human Services) in Waterbury, and it also processes Medicaid disability claims for the state.

virginia.state_note: Virginia DDS sits in the Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services (DARS) and decides medical eligibility for SSDI, SSI, and Medicaid disability claims, with district offices including Richmond, Norfolk, Roanoke, and Fairfax.

washington.state_note: Washington DDS is an agency of the Department of Social and Health Services with three regional offices in Olympia, Federal Way, and Spokane, and it also decides Non-Grant Medical Assistance disability claims.

west virginia.state_note: West Virginia's disability agency is the Disability Determination Section of the Division of Rehabilitation Services, with offices in Charleston and Clarksburg; West Virginia pays no state supplement to SSI.

wisconsin.state_note: Wisconsin's DDS is called the Disability Determination Bureau, in the Division of Medicaid Services of the Department of Health Services; it also decides disability for Wisconsin Medicaid and the Medicaid Purchase Plan.

wyoming.state_note: Wyoming's Disability Determination Services operates under the Wyoming Department of Workforce Services, with its office in Cheyenne at 5221 Yellowstone Road.
